10.1002_adfm.202417243: Fe‐based Prussian blue analogs (KFeHCF) are considered as the most promising cathode materials for potassium‐ion batteries (KIBs) owing to their low cost and high energy density. However, the unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) typically leads to rapid capacity decay upon long‐term cycling, thus limiting its practical application. Herein, for the first time, a dual‐additive strategy has been proposed as an effective and economical approach to regulate the interphase chemistry on KFeHCF surface. The optimized contents of potassium selenocyanate (KSeCN, 0.5 wt.%) and lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB, 0.5 wt.%) synergistically lead to the formation of a robust, homogeneous, and conductive CEI film, which promote charge transfer and K+ diffusion, inhibit side reactions and Fe dissolution, and realize stabilization of KFeHCF structure upon long cycling. As a result, the K∥KFeHCF battery with 0.5 wt.% LiDFOB + 0.5 wt.% KSeCN addition exhibits significantly improved cycling performance with a high capacity retention ratio of 81.5% after 5000 cycles at 500 mA g−1 current density and 4.5 V cutoff voltage. This study provides a new paradigm for designing high performance potassium‐ion battery via dual electrolyte additive incorporation.
10.1016_j.applthermaleng.2026.130440: Ternary lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) can experience hazardous temperature excursions even under normal cycling, posing significant safety risks. Herein, the coupled electro-thermal response of 26,650-type ternary LIBs are investigated subjected to oven-induced heating until thermal runaway (TR) under galvanostatic discharge (1C) at ambient temperatures of −25 °C, 0 °C, 25 °C, 50 °C, and 75 °C, respectively. High-speed videography and post-mortem analysis correlate macroscopic venting/flaming behaviors with microstructural changes in both residual electrodes and ejected materials. The heating-to-runaway process are delineated into four distinct stages based on synchronized voltage and surface temperature records. A consistent voltage dip point emerges 89 ± 5 s prior to TR onset across all these conditions, demonstrating its potential as a robust early-warning signature. With increasing ambient temperature, vented flames intensify markedly, producing larger burn areas and more severe casing deformation. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals C, O, Al, Ni, Co, Mn, and F in both ejecta and residual electrode materials. Notably, the relative carbon content in ejecta increases monotonically with ambient temperature, implying a temperature-dependent carbonization extent. These results provide quantitative benchmarks for optimizing thermal management strategies and defining safe operating envelopes for ternary LIBs across diverse climatic conditions. • Revealed four phases exist in the behavior of ternary batteries during discharge thermal runaway. • Ambient temperature rise enhances thermal runaway flame intensity and casing damage. • Ejecta carbon content rises with the increases of ambient temperature and indicating the carbonization. • Different ambient temperatures affects the microstructure of electrodes and ejected particles during discharge thermal runaway. • Quantified the V dp , T SVO , and T onset of discharge thermal runaway at different temperatures.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123338: Ultrasonic inspection has been recognised as one of the promising non-destructive evaluation (NDE) techniques for assessing the condition of Lithium-ion batteries (LiBs). However, the limited size of batteries causes guided waves to overlap, reducing the precision of conventional time of flight (ToF) and amplitude-based indicators. In this paper, a frequency–wavenumber ( f-k ) based index E f − k is proposed to address this limitation. In addition, a numerical finite element model incorporating lithiation-induced property variations is developed to simulate guided wave propagation across different states of charge (SoCs), further revealing the underlying mechanism during lithiation. An experimental study shows that in pouch-type LCO batteries, the wavenumber k P of the anti-symmetrical mode (A mode) decreases with battery charging. This trend is primarily associated with a significant increase in the shear modulus of the anode and a reduction in its compacted density. Simultaneously, the decrease in E f − k reflects increased wave attenuation due to elevated fluid content and enhanced microstructural heterogeneity in both the anode and cathode. A comparative analysis of ToF, amplitude, k P and E f − k index reveals distinct characteristics: ToF exhibits a clear but weakly sensitive trend with relatively low variability, whereas amplitude shows high sensitivity but suffers from substantial variability due to wave overlap. The wavenumber k P demonstrates moderate sensitivity with high reliability, particularly in the mid-to-high SoC range. E f − k index achieves an optimal balance between sensitivity and reliability, highlighting its potential for guided-wave-based LiB diagnostics.
10.1021_acs.analchem.5c02424: Nuclear magnetic resonance is the most conventional approach to characterizing the molecular weight ( M w ) of supramolecular polymers (SPs) at high monomer concentrations. However, it remains a great challenge to determine SPs with lower M w values because the increased monomer concentrations will assemble dynamically to larger SPs. In this contribution, we developed an SP-regulated electrochemiluminescence (ECL) strategy for differentiating the M w of SPs in low monomer concentrations. It was found that the SPs with lower M w could serve as a coreaction accelerator to provide larger electrochemically active surface areas and promote the oxidation process of coreactant tripropylamine (TPrA), resulting in improved ECL intensity. Therefore, a novel ECL platform has been successfully established to differentiate the M w of SPs at lower monomer concentrations. Our finding not only offers a deep understanding of the SP-regulated ECL performances but also provides the possibility for differentiating the M w of SPs via coreaction accelerator-mediated ECL, particularly in low monomer concentrations.
10.1021_acs.est.6c06646: Traditional toxicological testing cannot meet regulatory demands for numerous chemicals in aquatic environments. New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) such as High-Throughput Screening (HTS) and Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) framework offer sustainable alternatives. Here, we built a comprehensive Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) prediction and risk assessment framework that integrates a multidomain deep learning model, applicability domain assessment, and toxicity risk prioritization. Specifically, by applying in vitro HTS bioactivity to multiple Molecular Initiating Events (MIEs) and Key Events (KEs) in Daphnia magna AOP network, we compiled a data set (6971 chemicals × 10,024 multidimensional structure descriptors) exhibiting high chemical structural diversity and strong representativeness of environmentally relevant chemicals. QSAR prediction models covering application domains of multiple MIEs/KEs were further developed. The 6971 chemicals were risk-prioritized based on the AOP network topology, with the ranking results consistent with existing toxicological evidence. In addition, chemicals with potential combined toxic risks were identified. An out-of-the-box aquatic toxicity prediction and risk assessment tool is provided, enabling automated multitarget bioactivity prediction, reliability and decidability evaluation, and toxic risk profiling for new chemicals. This study represents a concrete application of "AI for Science" in ecotoxicology, aiming to reduce the dependence on traditional animal experiments. It simplifies the identification of potential toxic effects and bypasses in vivo validation processes to advance the sustainable management of environmental chemicals.
10.1021_acsami.2c19867: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), particularly the ones based on PEDOT:PSS, are excellent candidates for chemical and biological sensing because of their unique advantages. Improving the sensitivity and stability of OECTs is crucially important for practical applications. Herein, the transconductance of OECT is improved by 8-fold to 14.9 mS by doping the PEDOT:PSS channel with plasmonic gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) using a solution-based process followed by photo annealing. In addition, the OECT also possesses high flexibility and cyclic stability. It is revealed that the doping of AuNPs increases the conductivity of PEDOT:PSS and the photo annealing improves the crystallinity of the PEDOT:PSS channel and the interaction between AuNPs and PEDOT:PSS. These changes lead to the increase in transconductance and cyclic stability. The prepared OECTs are also demonstrated to be effective in sensitive detection of glucose within a wide concentration range of 10 nM-1 mM. Our OECTs based on photo-annealed plasmonic AuNP-doped PEDOT:PSS may find great applications in chemical and biological sensing, and this strategy may be extended to prepare many other high-performance OECT-based devices.
10.1038_s41563-024-01819-x: Hybrid organic/inorganic materials have contributed to solve important challenges in different areas of science. One of the biggest challenges for a more sustainable society is to have active and stable catalysts that enable the transition from fossil fuel to renewable feedstocks, reduce energy consumption and minimize the environmental footprint. Here we synthesize novel hybrid materials where an amorphous oxide coating with embedded organic ligands surrounds metallic nanocrystals. We demonstrate that the hybrid coating is a powerful means to create electrocatalysts stable against structural reconstruction during the CO 2 electroreduction. These electrocatalysts consist of copper nanocrystals encapsulated in a hybrid organic/inorganic alumina shell. This shell locks a fraction of the copper surface into a reduction-resistant Cu 2+ state, which inhibits those redox processes responsible for the structural reconstruction of copper. The electrocatalyst activity is preserved, which would not be possible with a conventional dense alumina coating. Varying the shell thickness and the coating morphology yields fundamental insights into the stabilization mechanism and emphasizes the importance of the Lewis acidity of the shell in relation to the retention of catalyst structure. The synthetic tunability of the chemistry developed herein opens new avenues for the design of stable electrocatalysts and beyond.
10.1039_d3ta05711a: Cobalt-imidazole-tetracarboxylate metal–organic framework (Co-MOF) and further modified with graphene (G) as heterogeneous electrocatalyst displays a bifunctional electrocatalytic performance towards ORR/OER.
10.1039_d6ta07471e: This review organizes single-atom catalyst functions in sodium-based batteries into two main categories: transport and interfacial processes, and redox chemistry regulation, highlighting design principles for each function.
10.1088_2752-5724_ae0c77: The disordered crystal growth and undesired degradation of perovskite films limit the further improvement of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) performance and their commercialization. Herein, an in situ modulation strategy is proposed for preparing high-quality and stable perovskite films by adjusting phase transformation kinetics. Benefiting from the in situ reaction between the chloroformamidinium hydrochloride (ClFACl) and FA cations, the impurity intermediate phase in the perovskite film is inhibited and the α -FAPbI 3 phase is induced to grow along a preferred (001) orientation. Furthermore, the introduction of ClFACl and the in situ formation of guanidinium salts (FA–Gua) strengthen the intermolecular interactions in the interior regions of crystals, restraining the α -phase degradation of the as-prepared perovskite films under humid and thermal treatments. With crystal orientation optimization and defects reduction, the PSCs with in situ formed FA–Gua yields a champion efficiency of 25.85% and demonstrates excellent phase stability under long-term thermal and humid aging conditions. This in situ chemical modulation strategy expands the avenue toward the optimization of crystallization orientation and α -phase stabilization, promoting the development of PSCs with enhanced performance and stability.
